population.definition: Monrovia (urban Montserrado County), rounded figure of 1.76 million reported by a fact-check citing the 2022 census thematic report on population projections; the exact LISGIS table could not be read (LISGIS pages need JavaScript)

source.title: Fact Check: Simeon Freeman Is Mostly Correct About Urban Population Growth
source.quote: Monrovia grew from 1.01 million people in 2008 to 1.76 million in 2022

facts.claim: Monrovia is named in honour of James Monroe, fifth president of the United States, and was founded by freed enslaved people who wished to establish a new country in Africa.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Named in honor of the fifth president of the United States (US), James Monroe , Monrovia was originally founded

facts.claim: The city is built on a cluster of small islands and peninsulas, with lagoons fed by the Mesurado River.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Built on a cluster of small islands and peninsulas, the city’s lagoons are fed by the Mesurado River

facts.claim: Bushrod Island, east of the city centre, holds the capital's deepwater port and most of its industrial infrastructure.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Bushrod Island, which features the capital’s deepwater port and contains the bulk of the capital’s industrial infrastructure

facts.claim: Monrovia has a rainy season lasting from May through October.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: The city also has a rainy season lasting from May through October.

facts.claim: In the 1960s improvements to Monrovia's port and ship repair facilities made it home to one of the world's largest fleets of ocean-going merchant vessels.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: During the 1960s, improvements to Monrovia’s port and to local ship storage and repair facilities made the port home to one of the world’s largest fleets of ocean-going merchant vessels.

facts.claim: Monrovia is still recovering from the 2014-15 Ebola epidemic, which prompted foreign investors and companies to leave Liberia and diverted government funds from public investment.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: It is also recovering from the 2014–15 Ebola epidemic, which prompted foreign investors and companies to leave the country and diverted government funds from public investment.

facts.claim: Liberia's urban population grew from 1.63 million in 2008 to 2.86 million in 2022, and the census report names Monrovia and Montserrado County as the principal destinations for migrants.

source.title: Fact Check: Simeon Freeman Is Mostly Correct About Urban Population Growth
source.quote: grew from 1.63 million in 2008 to 2.86 million in 2022 ... The report identifies Monrovia and Montserrado County as Liberia’s principal destinations for migrants

facts.claim: Monrovia was nearly destroyed in the civil wars: the first Liberian civil war (1989-96) was followed by a second (1999-2003) that further devastated the city.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: the second Liberian civil war (1999–2003) broke out, further devastating the already crumbling city

timeline.claim: In December 1821 the American Colonization Society acquired a strip of coast between the Mesurado and Junk rivers for trade goods valued at US$300.

source.title: Liberia: The Early Colony (Library of Congress Country Study, 1985)
source.publisher: GlobalSecurity.org reproduction of the US Library of Congress Country Study
source.quote: the ACS acquired a strip of land stretching 60 miles along the coast between the Mesurado and junk rivers in exchange for trade goods valued at US$300

timeline.claim: A small party took possession of Providence Island in the mouth of the Mesurado, and in April 1822 the first permanent settlement was established on the mainland near present-day Monrovia.

source.title: Liberia: The Early Colony (Library of Congress Country Study, 1985)
source.publisher: GlobalSecurity.org reproduction of the US Library of Congress Country Study
source.quote: took possession of Providence Island in the mouth of the Mesurado ... in April 1822 the first permanent settlement was established on the mainland

timeline.claim: Former enslaved people arrived at Providence Island, now Monrovia, in 1822 as part of an American Colonization Society mission.

source.title: Liberia kicks off bicentennial celebrating arrival of Black Americans
source.quote: The former slaves arrived in Providence Island, now the capital Monrovia, in 1822, as part of a mission by the American Colonization Society.

timeline.claim: The National Museum of Liberia was established by President William V. S. Tubman.

source.title: The National Museum of Liberia
source.quote: Established by the 18th president of the Republic of Liberia ... Tubman in 1958

timeline.claim: Improvements to Monrovia's port made it home to one of the world's largest fleets of merchant vessels.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: During the 1960s, improvements to Monrovia’s port and to local ship storage and repair facilities made the port home to one of the world’s largest fleets of ocean-going merchant vessels.

timeline.claim: A civil war broke out between the forces of Samuel Doe and supporters of Charles Taylor.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: In 1989, tensions again came to a head, resulting in a civil war between Doe’s forces and the supporters of Charles Taylor

timeline.claim: The second Liberian civil war broke out soon after the first ended and further devastated the city.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: the second Liberian civil war (1999–2003) broke out, further devastating the already crumbling city

timeline.claim: The National Museum has been housed in the Old Supreme Court building since 1987.

source.title: The National Museum of Liberia
source.quote: now housed in the Old Supreme Court building since 1987

timeline.claim: The Ebola epidemic struck Monrovia and Liberia, prompting foreign investors to leave.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: the 2014–15 Ebola epidemic, which prompted foreign investors and companies to leave the country

timeline.claim: The Monrovia City Council began erecting modern market tables at the Waterside general market.

source.title: Govt. erects steel tables for marketers
source.quote: has begun erection of modern market tables for marketers at the Waterside general market

places.name: Providence Island
places.what: Providence Island, in the mouth of the Mesurado, is where the founders of Monrovia first arrived in 1822 as part of an American Colonization Society mission. A cultural center now stands there.

facts.value: point of arrival of the founders of Monrovia

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro

source.quote: When Monrovia’s founders made their historic 1822 journey to the African coast, they first arrived on Providence Island

places.name: National Museum of Liberia
places.what: Established in 1958 and housed in the Old Supreme Court building since 1987, the museum lost around 5,000 artefacts during the wars and is rebuilding its collection. It was renovated in 1992 with international assistance.

facts.label: Established
facts.value: 1958, by President William V. S. Tubman

source.title: The National Museum of Liberia
source.quote: Established by the 18th president of the Republic of Liberia ... Tubman in 1958

source.title: The National Museum of Liberia
source.quote: now housed in the Old Supreme Court building since 1987

facts.label: War losses
facts.value: around 5,000 artefacts lost during the wars

source.title: The National Museum of Liberia
source.quote: The museum suffered the loss of around 5000 artefacts during the fourteen years of war and is still rebuilding its collection.

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro

source.title: Museum tells Liberia's story
source.quote: it was once home to almost 6,000 pieces for display and had a UNESCO-devised plan to make it one of the best museums in West Africa

places.name: Waterside Market
places.what: Waterside is a major market of Monrovia where, among many other items, African batik crafts and woodcarvings are sold. In 2020 the city council cleared makeshift stalls and began erecting modern market tables.

facts.label: Goods
facts.value: African batik crafts and woodcarvings among many other items

source.title: Monrovia, Liberia (Research Starters)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: the Waterside Market, where, among many other items, African batik crafts and woodcarvings are sold

facts.label: 2020 clearance
facts.value: police demolished makeshift stalls near the street

source.title: Liberia: Waterside Market Shuts Down Amid Rioting Fears
source.author: Webster Clayeh
source.quote: The Monrovia City Police on Sunday demolished several makeshift stalls in the market, especially the ones very close to the street.

facts.label: 2020 new tables
facts.value: City Council erected modern market tables

source.title: Govt. erects steel tables for marketers

notNotFound: Exact census count for Monrovia city proper (2022): LISGIS report and thematic reports are JavaScript pages (UNREADABLE); only the rounded 1.76 million figure from a Liberian fact-check citing the census thematic report was verified. Other figures (1,761,032; 2,225,911 metro) appear only on Wikipedia-derived pages.

Providence Island, National Museum and Waterside have no official city-government or museum page that was readable; sources are press and a reference database (EBSCO Research Starters, tier encyclopedia).
Many pages (UNESCO, Liberian Observer, Met Museum, History Today) returned 403/429/404 and were not used.
No well-sourced myth-or-fact item found for Monrovia.
